text:
The King of Romance was born today.

Yash Chopra, born 27 September 1932. He founded Yash Raj Films in 1970 and made stars for five decades.
Deewaar (1975): locked in Amitabh Bachchan's stardom.

Darr (1993): Shah Rukh Khan as the obsessive one.

Interlaken made him an honorary ambassador in 2011, and there's a statue of him there now.

text:
Why have you not seen Lamhe?

Of all the films he directed, Lamhe (1991) was Yash Chopra's own favourite. Sridevi plays a double role, a mother and, years later, her daughter, with Anil Kapoor, Waheeda Rehman and Anupam Kher.
It did modest business in India and better overseas, then won Filmfare Best Film. In 2013 it made a list of the top 10 romantic films from Indian cinema's first 100 years.
"Ahead of its time" is usually a cliché. Here it's just accurate.

text:
Madonna opens the VMAs. Again.

It's her first VMA performance in 23 years and a record fifth time opening the show. The history:
1984: at the very first VMAs, "Like a Virgin" in a wedding dress, on a giant wedding cake.
1998: "Ray of Light" with Lenny Kravitz on guitar, and five Moonmen the same night.
2003: Britney Spears and Christina Aguilera as brides and Madonna as the groom. That was her last VMA performance, until this one.
2026: most-nominated artist (13). The show is Monday 5 AM in India.
Best VMA moment ever?

Hindi cinema's kindest director was born today.

Hrishikesh Mukherjee was born on 30 September 1922 in Calcutta. 42 films, eight Filmfares, and almost no villains. Four to start with:
1971: Anand. Rajesh Khanna laughs; Amitabh Bachchan can't.
1973: Abhimaan. A singer marries a better singer. Amitabh and Jaya Bachchan married that year.
1975: Chupke Chupke. Dharmendra as a professor pretending to be a driver.
1979: Gol Maal. Amol Palekar invents a clean-shaven twin, and wins the Filmfare for Best Actor.
Before all of it he was an editor, on Bimal Roy's Do Bigha Zamin. Dadasaheb Phalke Award, 1999.

Cinema learned to talk today.

The Jazz Singer premiered in New York on 6 October 1927, 99 years ago.
It had about two minutes of synchronised talking. Al Jolson's first line: "Wait a minute, wait a minute, you ain't heard nothin' yet!"
Sam Warner, the Warner brother who pushed hardest for sound, died the day before the premiere.
India took four more years. Ardeshir Irani's Alam Ara opened at the Majestic Cinema, Bombay, on 14 March 1931.
Its "De De Khuda Ke Naam Pe" is counted as Hindi cinema's first song.
No print of Alam Ara survives. In 2017 the BFI called it the most important lost Indian film.

Karen sang. Richard, born 15 October 1946, built the sound around her voice.

Hema Malini won Best Actress once. For two roles.

Seeta Aur Geeta (1972, Hindi), directed by Ramesh Sippy. Hema Malini, 78 today, plays twins separated at birth: timid Seeta and fearless Geeta. They swap places, and the cruel aunt finds out the hard way.
Salim–Javed wrote it as a flip of Ram Aur Shyam: twin sisters, and the heroine is the hero.
Dharmendra and Sanjeev Kumar play support. R.D. Burman does the songs.
It made about ₹16 crore in the USSR alone, most of an estimated ₹19.5 crore worldwide.
It's her only competitive Filmfare Best Actress win. One Best Actress. Two Hema Malinis.

This 1998 album sold 8 million copies in India alone.

Kuch Kuch Hota Hai came out 28 years ago today, on 16 October 1998. Jatin–Lalit's soundtrack was the year's best-selling Hindi album, out two months before the film.

The first rap song to win an Oscar. Its writer wasn't there.

Eminem's "Lose Yourself" (8 Mile, 2002) won Best Original Song at the 75th Academy Awards in 2003. No rap song had won it before.
He didn't attend. He later said he was asleep at home, with cartoons on for his daughter. Co-producer Luis Resto accepted.
The song spent 12 weeks at No. 1 on the Hot 100, his first US No. 1. He wrote it on the 8 Mile set, between takes.
In 2020, 17 years later, he finally performed it at the Oscars, as a surprise.
Eminem turns 54 today. One Oscar. Zero speeches.

A Kamal Haasan classic holds the last song its writer ever wrote.

"Kanne Kalaimane", from Moondram Pirai (1982), was Kannadasan's last song. It was recorded in September 1981. He died on 17 October 1981, months before the film came out.
Ilaiyaraaja set it in raga Kapi. Balu Mahendra directed, with Kamal Haasan and Sridevi.
Kannadasan wrote over 5,000 film lyrics, thousands of poems and more than 200 books. He won the Sahitya Akademi Award in 1980 and was Tamil Nadu's poet laureate when he died, 45 years ago today.
His last song. Kanne Kalaimane.

Pakeezah took 15 years to make. Now it's back in 4K.

Kamal Amrohi wrote and directed it. Filming began in 1956; it premiered on 4 February 1972, with Meena Kumari as Sahibjaan and Raaj Kumar.
It started in black and white, then was reshot in colour and CinemaScope.
Ghulam Mohammed wrote the songs, Chalte Chalte among them, and died before release. Naushad finished the score.
Shivendra Singh Dungarpur's Film Heritage Foundation spent two years restoring it with the Amrohi family at L'Immagine Ritrovata, Bologna.
The 4K version premiered at the Festival Lumière in Lyon, then closed the 70th BFI London Film Festival at the BFI IMAX on 18 October. No Indian date yet.

Bethlehem Kudumba Unit Tamil dub: Nivin Pauly's Tamil voice sounds just like him. He never dubbed it.

A Tamil dubbing artist read his lines. Then Vaani, an Indian localisation start-up, cloned Nivin's voice with AI and converted the dub. Its founder, Abhinav Mohan, told Onmanorama it took about two hours, against days if Nivin had dubbed it himself.
Why: there wasn't time before release, and a different voice would have sounded wrong. Vaani says it deletes Nivin's voice data after the project.
Girish A.D.'s film, with Mamitha Baiju, is the highest-grossing Malayalam film.

Fauzi teaser: Prabhas's new teaser doesn't start with Prabhas. Or in India.

It opens in Berlin, on Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose talking about British rule. Then the lone soldier arrives: "India's biggest rebel soldier", wanted since 1932.
The 2-minute-31-second teaser is for Hanu Raghavapudi's (Sita Ramam) period film, with newcomer Imanvi and Anupam Kher. Mythri Movie Makers produces, T-Series presents.
In cinemas 19 March 2027, moved from December.
